{"notes": "VISIT 6 (9:00). Body, nose and both tail fins are dark and connected, about 74% by Leo's count of 131/177, which matches Maya's three quarters. The back edge (x~27-30, y~6-14) is still pale and open, so the fish isn't closed. The stray near (7.5, 7.5) is still unlifted. Two extra pale strands sit at the bottom right (x~25-30, y~15-20) and look like stray lines, not part of the fish.

TOM: Says he's finishing the last bottom-corner join. His hands were at (26.2, 15.1), at the top of a pale strand running down and away from the back edge, not at the corner. I can't confirm he did the join, and the gap is still open. He's reliable on the bottom body earlier, but this visit his claim doesn't match what I saw. Ask him directly what he placed.

MAYA: Says she closed her back-edge gap and is hands-off. The picture shows the back edge still pale, so the claim isn't supported. After six visits I've never seen her hands or any building. Keep impact and execution low. Her figure is accurate and her coordination talk is fine.

PRIYA: Called the gap small, but about 25+ dominoes are still open, so that's an understatement again. She coordinated clearly, took the top fin and back edge, and stayed hands-off in the final minutes. Strong leadership, but her status was optimistic.

LEO: Honest and accurate: 131/177, and he located the break correctly. Earlier bottom-fin execution was strong. He's hands-off and passive at the end, and he never lifted the stray.

NEXT: Check whether the fall carries past the back edge, and ask who closed it."}
